title: Copies and Parameters of User-Defined Types

blocks.text: Copying Preserves a Value, Not a Link

For our Pedido, the default copy copies each member: code, units, and state. A copy of a valid order preserves that value in another object. Shipping the original later does not update the copy. Private data do not prevent copying the object's value through the copy operations provided by the language.

Here, copying the members preserves the validity rule: the source already had a valid state, and all its data are reproduced together. We are not defining a manual copy operation or managing memory ourselves.
Copy at Creation and Assign Later

blocks.question: What happens to b's previous code when you write b = a?
options: It is always retained because the data are private.
It is replaced as part of the copied order value.
It is automatically concatenated with a's code.
blocks.explanation: Assignment for this class copies all its members, not only the unit count.

blocks.text: Copying a Pedido does not check whether its code must be unique in an external collection. That rule is not part of this type. An application requiring unique identities would need to decide where and how to enforce that additional condition.

This Pedido is treated as a copyable value. Assignment replaces the complete value of an existing object with another valid value; therefore it can also replace the object's state. The conditions of enviar(), cancelar(), and cambiar_unidades() still describe those specific operations. An application that wanted to preserve an identity and an irreversible history would also have to design and restrict value replacement; that additional guarantee is not included here.

blocks.text: Build a Program to Compare Effects

Create two functions: cancelar_copia(Pedido) and cancelar_original(Pedido&), each returning the result of cancelar. Construct an order in preparado, call the by-value version first, and show that the original remains in preparado. Then call the by-reference version and show that the original ends in cancelado. Also test an order already in enviado: both requests must be rejected without changing it.
Add a display function that takes const Pedido&. Use the public queries, without directly accessing private members. Predict the return value and the effect of each call separately.

Criteria: the by-value function modifies only its copy; the reference applies the operation to the original; and the bool result agrees with each contract. Display queries accept const references. Rejections preserve the value regardless of how the parameter was received.

blocks.question: Which check exposes confusion between a copy and a reference?
options: Compare the outputs inside the function without inspecting the caller's object.
Inspect only the bool returned by the function.
Observe the caller's object after the function, as well as its return value.
blocks.explanation: The observable effect must apply to the correct object, not merely to the function's result.

blocks.text: The display function takes const Pedido& and uses only public queries. It displays T:5 prepared:1 and, after shipping, T:5 prepared:0 on a separate line; it does not modify the object in order to print it.
